candidates.exact_span: Average of 15 or more neonates per surviving control female.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This numeric control-organism acceptance criterion governs whether a toxicity test result is valid for compliance comparison; a different reading of what counts as a surviving control female or how neonates are averaged could change whether an enforceable limit applies to a reported measurement.

candidates.exact_span: 60% of surviving control females must produce 3 broods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The brood-production threshold is an enforceable numeric QC criterion; interpreting surviving females, brood count, or the 60% requirement differently could change whether a toxicity measurement is treated as limit-bearing or excluded from compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Average dry weight per surviving organism in control must be ≥0.25mg.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This is a stated numeric minimum for control-organism dry weight; different interpretation of averaging method, surviving-organism definition, or unit could change whether a test result is deemed valid and subject to enforceable limit comparison.

candidates.exact_span: 40% or less, unless significant effects are exhibited.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The coefficient-of-variation cap includes a conditional exception tied to significant effects; whether the exception applies changes whether a test passes QC and therefore whether numeric compliance limits are operative for that monitoring period.

This PMSD range is a numeric acceptance bound for a sublethal endpoint; which column or endpoint it applies to, and how the inclusive range endpoints are read, could change whether a reported toxicity result is treated as exceeding an applicable limit.

This alternate PMSD range sits alongside another range in the same table; determining which range governs a given sublethal endpoint could change the applicable numeric criterion and compliance determination.

candidates.exact_span: If the flow from the outfall(s) being tested ceases during the collection of effluent samples, the requirements for the minimum number of effluent samples and the minimum number of effluent portions are waived during that sampling period. However, the permittee must collect an effluent composite sample volume during the period of discharge that is sufficient to complete the required toxicity tests with daily renewal of effluent, and must meet the holding time between collection and first use of the sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Discharge cessation triggers a partial waiver of sampling minima but retains composite-sample and holding-time duties; interpreting when flow has ceased, what sampling period is affected, or what volume is sufficient could change whether monitoring was required, was waived, or leaves a no-data state unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: When possible, the effluent samples used for the toxicity tests shall be collected on separate days.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The separate-days collection rule is a conditional monitoring protocol obligation; whether separate-day collection was possible or required affects whether applicable monitoring requirements were met or applicability remains unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: The effluent composite sample collection duration and the static renewal protocol associated with the abbreviated sample collection must be documented in the full report required in Item 3 of this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Documentation of abbreviated collection and renewal protocol is a permit condition tied to reduced sampling; whether adequate documentation exists affects whether conditional monitoring during low-flow or abbreviated periods is established as performed, not required, or evidence-deficient.

candidates.exact_span: Test failure may not be construed or reported as invalid due to a coefficient of variation value of greater than 40%, or a PMSD value greater than the higher value on the range provided.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This limits when QC exceedances invalidate a toxicity test; interpreting construe, reported, or higher value on the range differently could change whether a measurement is compared against discharge limits or classified as missing/invalid evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The statistical analyses used to determine if there is a significant difference between the control and the critical dilution shall be in accordance with the methods for determining the No Observed Effect Concentration (NOEC) as described in the appropriate method manual listed in Part II or the most recent update thereof.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The NOEC/significance methodology determines pass-fail against toxicity limits; choice among listed manuals or most recent update could change the computed significant-difference outcome and whether a measurement exceeds the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: Dilution water used in the toxicity tests will be receiving water collected as close to the point of discharge as possible but unaffected by the discharge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Receiving-water dilution is a baseline monitoring-protocol requirement; interpreting proximity, unaffected-by-discharge, or availability could change whether toxicity monitoring was required to proceed as specified or applicability is unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges to receiving water classified as intermittent streams
candidates.computation_change_reason: Intermittent-stream classification triggers substitution of synthetic dilution water; whether a discharge meets that classification changes applicable monitoring protocol and whether missing receiving-water samples reflect conditional non-requirement or unresolved obligation.

candidates.exact_span: toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges where no receiving water is available due to zero flow conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Zero-flow conditions authorize synthetic dilution water and bear on discharge-occurrence-dependent monitoring; interpreting zero flow or receiving-water availability could change whether monitoring was required, excused, or leaves a no-discharge/no-data state unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall substitute synthetic dilution water of similar pH, hardness, and alkalinity to the closest downstream perennial water for;
candidates.computation_change_reason: When substitution is triggered, the permittee must match pH, hardness, and alkalinity to the closest downstream perennial water; how similarity and closest perennial water are determined could change whether the monitoring protocol obligation was satisfied or remains unresolved.
